statements.status_notes: The upstream advisory states SQL injection can only occur when all four conditions hold: the non-default QueryExecModeSimpleProtocol is used, a dollar-quoted string literal is present in the query, that literal contains text that would be interpreted as a placeholder outside of a string literal, and the placeholder value is attacker-controlled. harbor-exporter reaches PostgreSQL using pgx/v4's default extended query protocol; QueryExecModeSimpleProtocol is never selected. The vulnerable code path therefore is not executed. pgx/v4 is on extended-maintenance-only upstream; the fix landed in pgx/v5, which would require Harbor to migrate its database layer.

GHSA-j88v-2chj-qfwx is fixed in pgx v5.9.2 but no fixed v4 release exists; pgx/v4 is in maintenance with no further security releases planned. The vulnerability requires a contrived combination of the non-default simple protocol, dollar-quoted string literals, and attacker-controlled placeholder text. Reachability through Telegraf's pgx/v4-using PostgreSQL plugins has not yet been audited; tracking with under_investigation pending that audit or migration of the dependency chain to pgx/v5.

GHSA-j88v-2chj-qfwx requires the non-default pgx simple protocol to be enabled. Harbor configures pgx via a standard DSN in src/common/dao/pgsql.go and never sets PreferSimpleProtocol or QueryExecModeSimpleProtocol, so the extended protocol (prepared statements) is always used and the dollar-quote placeholder confusion cannot occur.
